Register a flight in the time-series registry

Source: R/time_series.R
register_flight.Rd

Appends one row to the registry CSV. The flight_id is auto-generated from the date plus a short hash of the project directory, so repeated calls with the same date and project_dir are idempotent.

Usage

register_flight(
  date,
  project_dir,
  notes = "",
  registry_path = default_flight_registry(),
  odm_dataset_subdir = NA_character_,
  odm_project_name = NA_character_
)

Arguments

date

Date or character that as.Date() can parse.

project_dir

Project directory for the flight. Will be normalizePath-ed.

notes

Optional free-text notes.

registry_path

Path to the registry CSV. Defaults to default_flight_registry().

odm_dataset_subdir, odm_project_name

Optional ODM sub-project coordinates for this flight (as passed to dronebio_project()). Recorded so the flight can later be rebuilt with the exact ODM run that produced its products, rather than the micasense default. When left NA, flight_time_series() falls back to the dronebio_project() defaults.

Value

Invisibly returns the updated registry data frame.

Examples

# Registering a flight only records a path, so a throwaway directory is
# enough to demonstrate it; in practice project_dir is the ODM project
# directory produced by the flight.
reg <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
register_flight(date = Sys.Date(), project_dir = tempdir(),
                registry_path = reg)
list_flights(reg)
#>           flight_id       date     project_dir notes odm_dataset_subdir
#> 1 20260806-7b0e3d15 2026-08-06 /tmp/RtmpIdkppc    NA                 NA
#>   odm_project_name
#> 1               NA
